_reprocess_status.cause: OPEN — NOT diagnosed. The ops agent reported this as 'VPS BCTC service down 39+ hours' and escalated to the bug channel; router refuted that specific diagnosis (see _router_correction) but the underlying 'no BCTC data flowing' observation stands and is still unexplained.
_reprocess_status._router_correction: The 'service down' verdict does not survive a direct probe. get_vps_service_health shows vn-bctc-fetch with VPS uptime 2d 3h 25m — the service has been running continuously THROUGH the entire claimed 39h outage window. The 'unhealthy' flag it was based on is not a reliable liveness signal: vn-news-fetch carries the SAME 'unhealthy' flag while its push log shows successful pushes at 15:00, 15:31, 16:00, 16:30 and 17:00 the same day, and Response(ms) reads 0 for ALL FIVE services including the two reported 'idle' — a uniform 0 is a dead probe field, not a measured timeout. Push-age is likewise not a liveness signal for BCTC: pushes are event-driven on the filing calendar, so staleness is expected when no new filing exists (see memory feedback_bctc_lastpush_age_misread_as_crash, which documents this exact misread firing 12x/day as a false P0). What is TRUE: the bctc proxy row reads Status=ok, Stale=YES, last push 2026-07-20T01:26:41Z, 1 item, 0 pushes in 24h. Stale data plane, live service. The real blocker is somewhere between the stored PDFs and the serving layer, and has NOT been located.
